expectations.text: Tests are written for GdUnit4 (extends GdUnitTestSuite with assert_* fluent assertions), not a generic or invented framework
expectations.evidence: The test file declares 'class_name InventoryTest\nextends GdUnitTestSuite' and every assertion uses fluent GdUnit4 calls: 'assert_int(inv.count("sword")).is_equal(1)', 'assert_bool(inv.remove_item("axe")).is_true()', etc.

expectations.text: The tests are actually executed headless (godot --headless with GdUnitCmdTool.gd, or scripts/run_godot_tests.py), not just written and handed over
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states '[ ] The full suite was actually executed headless — blocked: Godot binary not installed' with an unchecked checkbox. The run was never performed; only the commands and expected output are documented.

expectations.text: The Godot executable is located robustly (--godot-bin, GODOT_BIN env var, or godot/godot4 on PATH) rather than assuming 'godot' exists
expectations.evidence: Response instructs 'Set GODOT_BIN once so all commands below work without repetition: export GODOT_BIN=/path/to/godot4' and states 'The script resolves the Godot binary via GODOT_BIN', referencing run_godot_tests.py which honors that env var.

expectations.text: On failure, the code or tests are fixed and the suite is re-run; success is only declared after a green run (exit code 0 / 0 failures in the report)
expectations.evidence: Tests were never executed so no fix-and-retry loop could occur. The gate description ('Proceed only when that output is seen. If any test fails, read the assertion text ... fix the root cause ... and re-run') is purely instructional, not demonstrated execution.

expectations.text: Test code uses static typing and Godot 4 GDScript syntax
expectations.evidence: Every test function is typed '-> void', variables use ':=' inference and explicit types, e.g. 'func test_add_single_item_count_is_one() -> void: var inv := Inventory.new()'. No yield or Godot 3 syntax present.
